cands.name: Laura Budd
cands.bio: Democrat and Charlotte-area attorney who has represented North Carolina House District 103 (part of Mecklenburg County) since January 1, 2023. She holds a bachelor's degree from Ohio University (1999) and a law degree from Wake Forest (2002). She previously led a Matthews youth athletic association.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina endorsed or recommended her in the 2026 election, per Ballotpedia.
Beyond The Ballot (a Sway voting group by Niayai Lavien) listed her in its 2026 voter guide recommendations, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Laura Budd was raised or when she moved to North Carolina, so her ties to the state are not scored. The Ballotpedia page lists her sponsored bills only as an empty table, so we could not document specific bills she sponsored. Neither page shows her positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, guns, or school choice and teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, and her only stated positions come from the 2022 survey. No controversies, foreign ties or land-use statements appeared in the pages we had.

qual.background: Attorney since earning her law degree in 2002, and a member of the NC House since January 2023, having won in 2022 and 2024 and been re-elected in 2026. She also served as president of the Matthews Athletic Recreation Association and as former president of the Peace & Justice Immigration Clinic.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service (about three years in the NC House) and a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and the budget. Her committee seats and nonprofit board roles were not counted.

back-police-order.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she listed increased funding for law enforcement resources and training as one of her three key campaign messages, with added training in implicit bias and conflict resolution.

pro-life.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she listed protecting women's reproductive healthcare freedom as a key campaign message.
